As a bonus action, you can expend a devil fruit usage to transform into your Full Beast Form, taking the form of the wild beast that inhabited the fruit you consumed. Your transformation lasts up to 10 minutes. This duration increases to 1 hour at 5th level, 8 hours at 10th level, 24 hours at 15th level, and unlimited at 20th level.

While in Full Beast Form, the following rules apply:

  • Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the Full Beast Stat Block you gain from the fruit, but you retain your alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the creature. The creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus in its stat block. If your physical stats are higher than that of your beast form, you can choose to retain them.

  • When you transform, you assume the beast’s hit points and Hit Dice. The hit points of the form scales with your level. For normal and carnivorous zoans it is calculated as (5 x your level) + your Full Beast’s Constitution modifier. For ancient zoans it is calculated as (6 x your level) + your Full Beast’s Constitution modifier. For mythical zoans it is calculated as (7 x your level) + your Full Beast’s Constitution modifier. When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. However, if you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form. For example, if you take 10 damage in Full Beast Form and have only 1 hit point left, you revert and take 9 damage. As long as the excess damage doesn’t reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren’t knocked unconscious.

  • You can speak to other animals of your species. You can still speak your regular language in this form.

  • You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal. Your equipment changes size or shape to match the new form.

  • You retain the benefit of any features from your class, race, or other source and can use them if the new form is physically capable of doing so. For example, using Extra Attack, Unarmored Movement, Strong Will, Rage, Experimental Medicine, etc.

  • Depending on the form, your ability to fulfill the somatic components of creations, use certain equipment like shields, or take actions that require the use of hands may be limited to the DM’s discretion, though through training this limitation may be overcome.

You have mastered a variety of special recipes, allowing you to prepare exotic dishes with useful effects. You gain the following benefits:

  • Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

  • You gain proficiency with cook’s utensils. If you are already proficient with them, you gain Expertise in them.

  • As an action, you can inspect a drink or plate of food within 5 feet of you and determine whether it is poisoned, provided that you can see and smell it.

  • As part of a short rest, you can cook special food, provided you have ingredients and cook utensils on hand. You can prepare enough of this food for a number of creatures equal to 4 + your proficiency bonus. At the end of the short rest, any creature who eats the food regains an extra 1d8 hit points.

  • With one hour of work or when you finish a short or long rest, you can cook a number of treats equal to your proficiency bonus. These special treats last 24 hours after being made. A creature can use a bonus action to eat one of those treats to gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Wisdom modifier.

All minks can generate electricity through their fur. Once per turn when you hit with a weapon attack, you can choose to deal lightning damage instead of the weapon's normal damage. When dealing lightning damage with this attack, the target then cannot take reactions until the start of your next turn.

You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can’t take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

Archery

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

Blind Fighting

You have &Reference[blindsight]{blindsight} with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn’t behind total cover, even if you’re blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

Defense

While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

Dueling

When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

Great Weapon Fighting

When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

Interception

When a creature you can see hits a target, other than you, within 5 feet of you with an attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage the target takes by 1d10 + your proficiency bonus (to a minimum of 0 damage). You must be wielding a shield or a simple or martial weapon to use this reaction.

Protection

When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a shield.

Superior Technique

You learn one maneuver of your choice from among those available to the Battle Master archetype. If a maneuver you use requires your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver’s effects, the saving throw DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

You gain one superiority die, which is a d6 (this die is added to any superiority dice you have from another source). This die is used to fuel your maneuvers. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest.

Thrown Weapon Fighting

You can draw a weapon that has the thrown property as part of the attack you make with the weapon.

In addition, when you hit with a ranged attack using a thrown weapon, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll.

Two-Weapon Fighting

When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

Unarmed Fighting

Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren’t wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8.

At the start of each of your turns, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to one creature grappled by you.

The powerful Brute focuses on the use of raw physical power honed to deadly perfection. Those who model themselves on this archetype combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows, and to take heavy hits.

Brute Force

Starting at 3rd level, whenever you hit with a weapon that you’re proficient with and deal damage, the weapon’s damage increases by 1d4. This feature also works with unarmed strikes. This bonus becomes 1d6 at 5th level, 1d8 at 11th level, and 1d10 at 17th level.

Unstoppable Durability

Beginning at 7th level, whenever you make a saving throw, roll 1d6 and add the die to your saving throw total. If applying this bonus to a death saving throw increases the total to 20 or higher, you gain the benefits of rolling a 20 on the d20.

Third Wind

At 10th level, you won't give up the fight. When you use your Second Wind feature, you additionally gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the amount you rolled.

Devastating Critical

Starting at 15th level, when you score a critical hit with a weapon attack, you gain a bonus to that weapon’s damage roll equal to your level in this class.

Survivor

At 18th level, at the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.

As a bonus action, you can expend a devil fruit usage to transform into your Hybrid Form, taking the shape that takes the best attributes of both your original body and the beast that now inhabits you. Your transformation lasts up to 10 minutes. This duration increases to 1 hour at 5th level, 8 hours at 10th level, 24 hours at 15th level, and unlimited at 20th level. This transformation ends early if you are killed, or if you end it as a free action.

While in Hybrid Form, you gain the following benefits:

  • When you enter the transformation, you gain temporary hit points equal to your level (double for regular and carnivorous zoans, triple for ancient zoans, and quadruple for mythical zoans).

  • All of your attacks deal an extra amount of damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

  • You gain any other features from your beast such as natural weapons, enhanced senses, multiple limbs, movement speeds, etc.

  • You can speak to other animals of your species. You can still speak your regular language in this form.

Starting at 2nd level, you can &Reference[push]{push} yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action.

Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.

Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

Description

A master of martial combat, skilled with a variety of weapons and armor

Hit Die: d10
Primary Ability: Strength or Dexterity
Saves: Strength & Constitution

Class Features

Level 1: Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d10 per fighter level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 10 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d10 (or 6) + your Constitution modifier per fighter level after 1st

Level 1: Proficiencies

Armor: All armor, shields
Weapons: Simple weapons, martial weapons
Tools: None
Saving Throws: Strength, Constitution
Skills: Choose two skills from &Reference[acr]{Acrobatics}, &Reference[ani]{Animal Handling}, &Reference[ath]{Athletics}, &Reference[his]{History}, &Reference[ins]{Insight}, &Reference[itm]{Intimidation}, &Reference[prc]{Perception}, and &Reference[sur]{Survival}

Level 1: Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) chain mail or (b) leather armor, longbow, and 20 arrows
  • (a) a martial weapon and a shield or (b) two martial weapons
  • (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) two handaxes
  • (a) a dungeoneer’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-classes.Item.QMrfJik92BnUZ9yL]{Level 1: Fighting Style}

You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can’t take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-classes.Item.ByNdCcF7p2n14zGd]{Level 1: Second Wind}

You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-classes.Item.Io5YdEto65nMzx8N]{Level 2: Action Surge}

Starting at 2nd level, you can &Reference[push]{push} yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action.

Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-classes.Item.2HZLPdjERSzxRCHd]{Level 3: Martial Archetype}

At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you strive to emulate in your combat styles and techniques. When you reach 4th level, and again at 6th, 8th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-classes.Item.eiWhaHo80fKtsbEN]{Level 5: Extra Attack}

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 11th level in this class and to four when you reach 20th level in this class.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-classes.Item.bHQTj9sOzHYOXVV5]{Level 9: Indomitable}

Beginning at 9th level, you can reroll a saving throw that you fail. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can’t use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

You can use this feature twice between long rests starting at 13th level and three times between long rests starting at 17th level.

Starting Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) chain mail or (b) leather armor, longbow, and 20 arrows
  • (a) a martial weapon and a shield or (b) two martial weapons
  • (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) two handaxes
  • (a) a dungeoneer’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack
Starting at 5th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing heavy armor.

You once were a chef, the king of food. Either you were an artisan chef with a fine sense of taste, a master chef who knows dozens on dozens of recipes by heart, or a cook at the mess hall, serving food quickly and on the double. You understand that food has a voice; it can express moods with the right combinations of ingredients, or bring people together with a peaceful meal. What brought you out of the kitchen and into the sea? A rare ingredient? Maybe your upper chef decided it was time for you to go? Or, maybe, you wanted to go on an adventure to discover the mythical All Blue ?Regardless of why you decided to change pace from your culinary solitude, your cooking and food-handling skills will prove vital to your crew.

Skill Proficiencies: 2 from Insight, Performance, and Sleight of Hand

Tool Proficiencies: Cooks Utensils

Equipment: 100,000 Berries; Mess kit; 15 Rations; and a recipe book; Cooks Utensils

Feature: Culinary Expert
Your mastery of culinary art has granted you the ability to cook special meals and treats for yourself and your crew. You gain your choice of the Gourmand Feat (Pg. 212) or the Master Brewer Feat (Pg. 217).

Suggested Characteristics

Chefs vary widely in temperaments. As professionals, they can be fickle and perfectionists who run their team ragged. However, they are also dedicated to their vocation and skill to ultimately fill up bellies and provide hospitality.
A backpack can hold one cubic foot or 30 pounds of gear. You can also strap items, such as a bedroll or a coil of rope, to the outside of a backpack.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.dMKfoZ0uGktZg8lk]{Level 10: Intimidating Presence}

If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a [[/save wis format=long]] (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.

If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can’t use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.2DHPsCquP046x3sz]{Level 14: Retaliation}

A punch, kick, head-butt, or similar forceful blow (none of which count as weapons). On a hit, an unarmed strike deals bludgeoning damage equal to 1 + your Strength modifier. You are proficient with your unarmed strikes.

Most zoans give the user natural weapons, such as the horns of a bull. For the sake of simplicity, any zoan weapon counts as both a natural weapon and unarmed strike.

There are various animals that zoans can transform into, such as various species of cats with regular zoans, extinct species such as dinosaurs with ancient zoans, and dragons from myth with mythical zoans.

  • When a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you (and that target doesn't have this feat), you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the attacking creature.
Rope, whether made of hemp or silk, has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

Due to your appearance being based upon an animal, you also gain their natural weapons, such as the claws of a lion, the teeth of a wolf, the horns of a ram, or even the fists of an ape. You have natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you can deal one of either bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength or Dexterity modifier. You can choose whether to use Strength or Dexterity when attacking with these natural weapons, but must use the same ability score for both the attack and damage roll.

You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

The mysterious mink tribe is a race of fur-covered, anthropomorphic humanoids from the "phantom island" of Zou in the New World, a moving island situated atop the back of an ancient, millenium old elephant known as Zunesha. Because of its unique location, Zou is impossible to find with a logpose, hiding the minks away from the eyes of the world as a result. While most humans go their entire lives without ever seeing a mink, the rumors of Zou's formidable sentinels carry far and wide across the new world, telling tales of the minks' mythical ability to wield electricity like a weapon and transform into vicious beasts beneath the light of the full moon.

Close-knit Community

The island of Zou rests on the back of a giant, millenia-old elephant known as Zunesha. Truthfully, however, despite having been hunted for slaves by human pirates in the past, minks are exceptionally welcoming and hospitable to all manners of visitors that come in good faith to their island.

Minks have a tight-knit community on their island, making no difference between themselves regardless of a mink's features. They show affection to eachother through physical contact or acts of generosity, having next to no concept of personal space even between relative strangers. "Garchu", a common practice among minks, consists of rubbing their temple or cheek against each other, signifying a greeting or act of gratitude.

Each individual mink takes after a specific fur-covered mammalian creature, and recognize differences in their kin by referring to canine minks as such, for example. However, mink do not differentiate from each other, and carnivorous minks live side by side with herbivorous minks. Mink society places a stigma on eating animals with fur, and as such their diet primarily consists of reptiles, fish and greens found on the island of Zou.

Moonlit Warriors

All minks tend to be stronger than normal humans, possessing formidable physical abilities typical to their animalistic side, such as strong legs that can scale trees in a single leap, or powerful muscles for physical labor. Their abilities do not remarkably deteriorate with age, and this combined with an effective metabolism and recovery rate makes them formidable fighters in battle.

Adding to that, minks have two additional abilities that serve to differentiate them from humans: Electro, the ability to generate powerful electrical charges through their fur, and Sulong, the ability to transform into an even more powerful form while under the light of the full moon.

Sulong is the most feared ability of the minks, known to transform them into unstoppable, rampaging beasts. Only a few minks master this ability, as loss of control can result in the death of not just their enemies, but their allies and even themselves as well. While transformed, a mink grows increasingly ferocious as their fur grows out, their muscles tense and their claws extend, becoming a frightful sight to behold by their enemies.

Mink Traits

As a mink, you have the following traits.

Ability Score Increase. One ability score of your choice increases by 2, and another one increases by 1. Alternatively, three ability scores of your choice increase by 1.

Age. Minks reach adulthood in their late teens and live as long as humans.

Alignment. Minks are generally gregarious and friendly, though they focus on their own community over contact with other races, making them lawful good.

Size. Minks vary greatly in size due to their animal heritage, but typically are comparable to humans. Your size is your choice of small or medium.

Speed. Your base walking speed is 35 feet.

Darkvision. You are accustomed to the dark forests of Zou. You have darkvision out to 60 feet and can see in dim light as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

Natural Weapons. Due to your appearance being based upon an animal, you also gain their natural weapons, such as the claws of a lion, the teeth of a wolf, the horns of a ram, or even the fists of an ape. You have natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you can deal one of either bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength or Dexterity modifier. You can choose whether to use Strength or Dexterity when attacking with these natural weapons, but must use the same ability score for both the attack and damage roll.

Inner Beast. You can draw upon your bestial blood to greatly boost your speed and strength for a short time. As a bonus action, you can grant yourself advantage on all Strength and Dexterity-based ability checks for 1 minute. During this time, your speed increases by 10 and when you use your Electro trait, you deal additional lightning damage equal to your level. You must finish a long rest before you can use this trait again.

If the full moon is visible when you make this transformation, you enter Sulong form for the duration, increasing both your Strength and Dexterity scores by 4. This increase can exceed an ability score of 20, but not 30. When this sulong form ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion.

Electro. All minks can generate electricity through their fur. Once per turn when you hit with a weapon attack, you can choose to deal lightning damage instead of the weapon's normal damage. When dealing lightning damage with this attack, the target then cannot take reactions until the start of your next turn.

Subrace. Choose between diurnal or nocturnal.

Diurnal

Diurnal minks are primarily awake and active during the day. Due to catching sunlight, they do most of the agricultural work among the mink.

Diurnal Nature. You gain proficiency in two of the following skills of your choice: Athletics, History, Medicine, Nature, or Persuasion.

Nocturnal

Nocturnal minks are primarily awake and active during the night. Owing to their nightly activities, they make excellent scouts and defenders.

Nocturnal Nature. You gain proficiency in two of the following skills of your choice: Acrobatics, Athletics, Perception, Stealth, or Survival.

Description

A fierce warrior who can enter a battle rage

Hit Die: d12
Primary Ability: Strength
Saves: Strength & Constitution 

Class Features

Level 1: Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d12 per barbarian level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 12 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d12 (or 7) + your Constitution modifier per barbarian level after 1st

Level 1: Proficiencies

Armor: Light armor, medium armor, shields
Weapons: Simple weapons, martial weapons
Tools: None
Saving Throws: Strength, Constitution
Skills: Choose two from &Reference[ani]{Animal Handling}, &Reference[ath]{Athletics}, &Reference[itm]{Intimidation}, &Reference[nat]{Nature}, &Reference[prc]{Perception}, and &Reference[sur]{Survival}

Level 1: Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a greataxe or (b) any martial melee weapon
  • (a) two handaxes or (b) any simple weapon
  • An explorer’s pack and four javelins

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.I2M4rEBd4RHtQd9u]{Level 1: Rage}

In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action.

While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren’t wearing heavy armor:

  • You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
  • When you make a melee weapon attack using Strength, you gain a bonus to the damage roll that increases as you gain levels as a barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian table.
  • You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

If you are able to cast spells, you can’t cast them or concentrate on them while raging.

Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious or if your turn ends and you haven’t attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on your turn as a bonus action.

Once you have raged the number of times shown for your barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian table, you must finish a long rest before you can rage again.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.jxpJ27LVPj5VrURu]{Level 1: Unarmored Defense}

While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.MnFxJixR9VUIdTYl]{Level 2: Reckless Attack}

Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.eA4YO3tPwcgBaLDJ]{Level 2: Danger Sense}

At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren’t as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger.

You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can’t be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.6HYs4bIGPnbFV0HB]{Level 3: Primal Path}

At 3rd level, you choose a path that shapes the &Reference[nat]{nature} of your rage. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th levels.

Level 4: Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.ZMimCCA9Jx1IULw1]{Level 5: Extra Attack}

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.rQe7O2MWTYq2qmwC]{Level 5: Fast Movement}

Starting at 5th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing heavy armor.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.4fNvfejx5cjjx0hW]{Level 7: Feral Instinct}

By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls.

Additionally, if you are surprised at the beginning of combat and aren’t incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn, but only if you enter your rage before doing anything else on that turn.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.bEOMpsg8JR7FTYJx]{Level 9: Brutal Critical}

Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack.

This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.KoKUf6qwe1Hjis9x]{Level 11: Relentless Rage}

Starting at 11th level, your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you’re raging and don’t die outright, you can make a [[/save con 10 format=long]]. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead.

Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a short or long rest, the DC resets to 10.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.4KgnKmDDh1esna6H]{Level 15: Persistent Rage}

Beginning at 15th level, your rage is so fierce that it ends early only if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.lJk2V8V2huKCrgle]{Level 18: Indomitable Might}

Beginning at 18th level, if your total for a [[/check str format=long]] is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

@UUID[Compendium.world.ddb-blood-and-brine-ddb-backgrounds.Item.w7sy1Ush4uft8MnC]{Level 20: Primal Champion}

At 20th level, you embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.

Starting Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a greataxe or (b) any martial melee weapon
  • (a) two handaxes or (b) any simple weapon
  • An explorer’s pack and four javelins

Firing in Melee. Being within 5 feet of an enemy doesn’t impose Disadvantage on your attack rolls with Ranged weapons.

Your attack rolls with Ranged weapons can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

Your attack rolls with Ranged weapons can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20 on the d20.

Your attack rolls with Ranged weapons can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 17-20 on the d20.

# CHAPTER 1 — ALICE![[Alice.png]]

Morning reached the Lunarian village gently, the way it always did—light spilling like molten gold over the high plateau, brushing the stone rooftops and silver-feathered banners that fluttered lazily in the wind. The sun rose close here, closer than anywhere else in the world; the village was perched at the very top of the Grand Line, seemingly carved into the heavens themselves.

“Alice,” her mother’s voice echoed through the small home, firm but not unkind. “Up. The council is gathering.”

Alice groaned into her blankets. She was twelve, and mornings were the enemy. “I’m awake… mostly,” she mumbled.

Her mother, Chieftain Blerta, leaned over her. Proud black wings folded neatly behind her, sunlight haloing her stern face. “You are my heir. You don’t have the luxury of lazy mornings.”

Alice sat up, rubbing her eyes, hair sticking in every direction. “I know, I know. I just… I liked it better when I wasn’t an heir.”

“That is not how inheritance works,” Blerta said, though Alice could hear a smile behind the words.

Outside, the village was alive. Warriors sparred in courtyards, children chased each other between looming sky-torches, and elders tended to gardens that grew along the cliff edges. Alice followed her mother to the council hall—a carved dome of obsidian and white skywood—its doors already open.

Inside, voices were tense.

“The caravans from Sea Gate haven’t returned in three days.”

“We’ve seen lights on the horizon—metallic, green-glowing. Not ships we recognise.”

“And scouts report masked men near the lower paths.”

Blerta raised a hand. Silence fell.

“Until we know more,” she said, “we prepare. Quietly. No panic.”

Alice watched them all. Every voice felt heavy, wary. She sucked in a breath—this wasn’t the usual talk about border disputes or harvest allocations. Something was wrong. Very wrong.

After the meeting, Alice shifted restlessly. “Mother… are we in danger?”

“All lands are always in danger.” Blerta rested a hand briefly on her shoulder. “But ours stands tall. Go to training. Show me you understand your duties.”

Alice joined the women warriors atop the sunlit terrace. Their black wings flashed like obsidian as they drilled forms. Alice, though young, moved with natural grace. Her punches were clean, her stance steady. The warriors whispered proudly—“She’ll surpass her mother someday.” Alice tried to hide her smile every time she overheard it.

After training, she rushed down the sloping path toward the fields. Malphas was there, as always, sleeves rolled up, digging through the soil with disciplined focus. Her older brother was quiet, patient, always thinking before he spoke—everything Alice was not.

She flopped down beside him. “Council meeting was boring.”

Malphas chuckled softly. “I’m sure Mother will be glad to hear that.”

“You’re supposed to agree with me.”

“I’m supposed to be the responsible one.”

“That’s my job now.”

“Well,” Malphas said, setting down his tools, “then you might want to stop throwing pebbles at my head.”

Alice froze mid-throw. “Oh.”

He flicked the pebble from her hand. “Come. Father should be at the gatehouse by now.”

They walked together toward the towering gate carved into the mountain’s edge. Their father Kreshnik stood watch, spear in hand, wings casting a long shadow. He greeted them with a warm nod. “My stars. Both of you together—should I be worried?”

“Always,” Alice said proudly.

He ruffled her hair. “Then I am prepared.”

Evening dipped toward night. Lanterns lit the pathways, families ate together, music drifted from the hearth-hall. It felt peaceful. Normal.

Until it didn’t.

A thundercrack split the air.

Alice jerked upward. Malphas froze. Their father took one step outside the gatehouse—and the sky tore open.

Three figures descended from above, walking on the air itself. Boots clicking on invisible steps. Coats whipping. One wore swirling white. Two others in sharp armoured suits—♾️.

The first villager screamed.

The attack began.

Energy blasts streaked downward, ripping through rooftops. Warriors leapt into the air but were shot from the sky. The three intruders moved like falling stars—fast, precise, merciless.

“Malphas!” their father roared. “Take your sister. RUN.”

Malphas grabbed Alice’s hand. She had never seen him scared. Not like this. They sprinted between shattered houses as the ground shook and fire licked the sky.

Behind them, adults were falling—elders, warriors, their mother’s council guards. Alice’s breaths came fast, sharp; her wings trembled violently.

They reached a narrow alley—then a dozen figures in white coats and gas masks slid from the shadows like ghosts.

“Targets confirmed. The Lunarian children,” one said, voice flat.

Malphas stepped in front of Alice, fists clenched. “Stay behind me.”

The masked men lunged. Malphas fought with desperate fury—punches cracking helmets, feet launching soldiers back. Alice swung wildly, cutting through two with the sharp edge of her wing. But there were too many.

A cannon round blasted from behind the attackers.

Alice didn’t see where it came from. She only saw the explosion swallow Malphas.

“NO!” she screamed as he was hurled across the stone.

Her pulse thundered. Rage, fear, grief twisted together. Something ancient roared awake inside her.

A wave burst out of her—a storm of will itself.

White coats collapsed instantly. Helmets cracked. Bodies hit stone. Even the torches flickered as if bowing.

Alice stood trembling, tears streaking down her face.

Then—

A hand clamped around her mouth.

A whisper slid into her ear:

“So the girl possesses the Color of the Supreme King. How… interesting.”

A pressure struck the back of her head.

Darkness swallowed her whole.

# CHAPTER 2 — CLINE “The Plague”

![[Cline 1.png]]

The sea had teeth that night. It tore at the wood and tossed the bodies like toys. Cline came to with salt in his mouth and the taste of iron on his tongue, the horizon a blur of black and pale foam. For a long, foggy second he believed the world was still water. Then rough hands hauled him over a rail and the deck lurched under him, throwing him face-first onto wet planks. He coughed until his ribs burned and the world steadied enough for him to see the shapes—two figures in masks leaning over him, their boots slick with seawater.

“Shouldn't we just let him die?” one of them said, the words swallowed by the hiss of their respirator.

“Why not?” the other answered like it was a comfortable choice. “We’ve cages to fill. He looks like he’ll fetch a coin.”

Cline tried to make his arms obey. He tried to curl, to make himself nothing. He had practiced this smallness his whole life—making himself small when the looks came, shrinking behind bales and husks of towns so strangers wouldn’t see the eyes. But the guards were efficient; they hauled him below, dragging his wet feet across the boards, and shoved him into a narrow cell with a clang of iron. Water dripped from his hair and pooled at his feet. The light in the cell was thin and smelled of oil and old metal.

Across from him, behind a second barred window, a figure sat with his back to the wall. Cline could not yet make out the features—just a silhouette, the slack of someone who had been held too long. He saw, later, how the moonlight touched the other man’s shoulders like a promise. For now he only knew the other prisoner breathed shallow and cautious, and a guard outside called, “Hey, Freak—wake up. We move you to your sister at dawn. Boss wants answers.”

The word “Freak” had always been a rope around Cline’s neck. He had been chased from one harbor to the next at that name. Children had thrown stones at him until he curled into a ball and the town dogs refused him shelter. He had tried to be useful—carrying water, mending nets, fixing shutters—only to be blamed when storms came, as if the sky itself hated him. The memory of one harbor boy’s fist, the gleam of fear in a woman’s eyes as she crossed to the other side of the lane, lived in him like a fossil. He had learned, painfully, that kindness was a currency he could not spend.

So when the guard beyond the bars leaned close to the other prisoner and mimicked kindly tones—“You’ll be singing for us soon enough, friend. Don’t be shy”—Cline felt something that was not merely sympathy. It was kinship and a corrosive knot of old shame. He pounded the iron with his fist. “Stop,” he called. His voice was small; the guard laughed and poked him with the butt of a baton.

“What are you doing?” the guard asked. “You want to be last for the crate? Quiet, freak.”

Cline backed away even as another part of him moved forward—an animal reflex to protect what could not be protected. He had spent years letting himself take the brunt, letting other hands hit him first to spare a startled child or a stranger’s pride. It was a coward’s logic and a martyr’s heart tangled into one. “Please,” he whispered, more a plea to the damp air than to the man. “Don’t—don’t hurt him.”

That was when the rod came down. It arced through the cell like a white snake. Cline felt the first strike in his shoulder and the sound of it was a small, traitorous thing—an electric pop that traveled through bone and made his teeth rattle. He cried out, not for himself but for the other prisoner, who flinched as if hearing the same fear. The guard sneered. “You’d get yourself killed for nothing? Pathetic.”

Another strike. Pain lanced across his chest. Cline clutched the iron bars and tasted bile. His skin went prickly, as if a swarm of insects skittered beneath it. The thing inside him, the thing he had learned to name only in the loneliest hours—Shadow, Curse, the Other—shifted and grew awake. It had always been there, in tremors and whispers: when a crowd hissed at him, a third eye of feeling opening somewhere behind his ribs. He had managed it by shrinking, by swallowing the urge to lash out. Tonight, under the battering of rods and the smell of salt and iron, control frayed.

“Stop it,” he begged and meant it for both the guards and whatever lived beneath his skin. “No more. Please—”

The dark answered like a mouth opening. It unfurled not with noise but with a pressure, a soundless tidal pull that tugged at the edges of the world. At first it was only a shadow at the corner of his vision, like smoke shaped into intent. Then it moved with terrible purpose, long and sinewy, seeping from his joints and through the weave of his clothes. Eyes, wet and glassy and alien, bloomed along his forearms and the inside of his elbow—dozens of them, blinking in a rhythm that tasted of old grief. The first guard’s laugh cut off in a short, strangled gasp.

“W—what is that—” the second guard began, but there was no time to finish. Something like a blade formed from the shadow, sharp as despair, and it slid across the deck with surgical grace. The first man’s body was bisected with a sound that was all wrong for the ocean: a clean, wet clap, and red geysering sent a fine rain over the planks. Time stuttered as the shadow retracted and a part of Cline felt, absurdly, embarrassment for the mess. Another part was flooded with release—an animal’s delighted relief at being unchained.

Terrified shouts ricocheted below decks as men scrambled. Lanterns tipped; boots slapped. The second guard reached for his own weapon and a tentacle of darkness smashed into his throat, cracking bone like a brittle twig. He landed with the wind knocked out of him, eyes popping and white. Blood painted the stripes of the hull. For a breathless moment the ship was a strange new weather: rain of red, a sky of shadow, and Cline at the center of both, fingers curled uselessly around empty air.

He did not mean to open the other cell. He did not mean to tear the lock free, to fling metal aside as if it were paper. He had meant only to stop them, to make them stop and listen. But the shadow did not ask permission. It shoved him, pushed and pulled and used his limbs like ropes. The bars gave with a shriek. The other prisoner—Cline saw him now plainly: young, hair matted, wings like a half-closed sail—was knocked backward by a wave of wind as the hatch exploded open.

“Run!” Cline heard, or thought he heard, but the voice was distant and not fully his. He saw the young man—Malphas—stagger to his feet, wide-eyed, and run for the broken steps that led to the deck. He did not see the speed or the grace he would later claim; he felt only the surge of sky under that figure’s feet as he launched, driven by desperation. The shadow made a reach and struck at the ankles, but Malphas pushed through the air like a boy surviving a storm and began to rise.

Around Cline everything was wrong and yet terribly precise: a face the color of wet ash, an arm sliced clean off and still twitching, a guard who had tried to hide behind a column now rolled into the gloom and did not rise. The shadow took meat and bone with a careful, indifferent hunger, and Cline, trapped inside, watched as much as he felt: the eyes on his skin blinking, tentacles unfurling and coiling, a blackness that smelled faintly of the deep sea and of old ironies.

When the last of the men stopped moving, the shadow pulled back as if sated. The world went silent in a way Cline had never known: no footfalls, no ragged breathing, only the drip of seawater from disrupted lanterns. He was spent—hollowed out, as if the light that defined him had been squeezed and wrung and thrown aside. He tried to speak and found only a cracked whisper. “I—” His voice broke. Guilt rolled over him in waves thicker than the sea. He had wanted to be the kind of man who took the blows and kept a clean conscience. Instead he had become what people had always feared. The guards’ blood felt too much like proof.

They were both gone—escapees and wreckage. Malphas was a shadow against the sky, flinging himself into the night and away from the smoking corpse of the ship. Cline watched him go, and among the cacophony of emotions something small and stubborn coalesced: relief. It was a shameful relief edged with a stab of longing, the twisted thing that had always ruled him. He had saved someone else, and in saving he had paid the bill the world demanded from him.

When he woke he was on a plank, the rim of it creaking in cold water. His skin felt stretched and foreign; the eyes that had covered his arms were gone, leaving pale scars like the lines of dried riverbeds. The ship that had once been a living thing was only ruins—a splintered skeleton smoking slowly in the moonlight. Somewhere far above, a dark shape cut across the sky and vanished into cloud. Cline tried to move and found his limbs heavy and clumsy, as if someone else had used them and forgotten to return the blueprints.

“Hey—hey you!” a voice called, closer now. Metal gleamed in the distance—white hull, blue pennant. A marine cutter had appeared as if conjured; its crew shouted and tossed ropes. Cline squinted into the lantern glow and saw men in uniform hauling him up. They checked him like an animal, hands quick and clinical. “You’re alive. Keep him warm,” one barked.

Cline let them. He let them lift him and wrap a frayed blanket around his shoulders. He closed his eyes and tried to fix the last image of Malphas in his mind: the tilt of his head as he rose, a hint of defiance in his shoulders, the thin line of sorrow that had crossed his face when he looked back. Cline thought, absurdly, of apology—he mouthed the word once, silent on the plank, a promise to a boy already far away.

The cutter pulled them toward the hold of the marine ship and the world turned bureaucratic: questions asked in sharp tones, a ledger scratched, bandages tied. Cline lay under a blanket and watched the stars, feeling like a planet with a scarred crust. The shadow inside him was quiet now, retreated like a tide. But the memory of its teeth and the taste of his own hands in blood would never truly fade. He had been the weapon and the wound both.

As the ship cut into the dark sea, Cline’s last clear thought before sleep took him was neither pride nor triumph. It was older and quieter: I don’t want to hurt anyone. I never wanted to be this. If I can, if I still can, I will carry the pain myself. I will take what the world wants to throw away so others can breathe.

But the ocean keeps records, and it cradles nothing perfectly. The plank underneath him rocked and creaked. Somewhere, far above the clouds, a shadow had wings.

# CHAPTER 3 — MALPHAS “The Waning Fist”

Malphas didn’t remember the fall.

He remembered the sky folding beneath him, wings faltering, blood roaring in his ears as exhaustion gouged him from the inside. He remembered Cline’s monstrous shadow ripping through the ship. Then—

Nothing.

He smashed through the canopy of a tropical island like a meteor with no flame. Branches shattered, stone cracked, and the world swallowed him in a crater of steaming earth. The impact tore consciousness from him like a thief plucking a coin.

For three days, he did not wake.

The islanders found him first. Hunters with feathers braided in their hair approached the crater cautiously. They took one look at the black wings, the charred feathers, the Lunarian markings—and dropped to their knees.

They whispered a single word in their dialect:

“Aru-Ka’to.”

The Thunder God Returned.

They carried his limp body to their village, a ring of huts beneath thunderclouds permanently hovering above the plateau. At night, lightning arced with unnatural precision, as though guarding something sacred. They laid Malphas on woven mats, cleaned his burns, wrapped his chest, fed him broth through trembling hands—terrified yet reverent.

But Malphas’s internal injuries were catastrophic. His pulse flickered weakly, his lungs burned like crushed embers. The healers whispered among themselves: even gods die.

So they gambled.

From a shrine carved into stone, guarded by seven warriors, they retrieved a radiant fruit—jagged, feathered, glowing faintly blue with threads of lightning crawling across its surface.

The Mythical Zoan: Thunder Bird.

They peeled it reverently, and one drop of its juice touched Malphas’s tongue.

Lightning erupted.

His back arched violently. Sparks danced across his skin. His feathers shimmered, every vein humming with a deep electric thrum. Storm clouds above gathered as though sucking in breath. When he gasped awake, the world itself seemed to exhale in relief.

The healers bowed so low their foreheads scraped the ground.

“You… soared again,” one whispered, voice trembling.

Malphas blinked, disoriented. His body felt different—lighter, sharper, thrumming with barely-contained energy. His heart beat twice, then once, then twice again—unstable, but powerful.

“I… need to go,” he rasped. “My sister… she—”

But the island did not give him time.

The first explosion shook the treeline. The second leveled a hut. Screams rose as masked figures moved through the smoke like ghosts—two of them, marked with the symbol of Libra, the balanced scales etched onto their jackets.

Malphas staggered to his feet, wings flaring open. “Stay behind me!” he shouted to the villagers.

Too late.

The bulky one—massive arms, reinforced armour—slammed his blades into Malphas’s ribs before he could react. The smaller one—lanky, flexible, eyes like needles—appeared behind him and clamped a seastone cuff around his wrist.

Malphas roared, lightning spasming from his fingertips, but the seastone drained him instantly. His knees hit the ground. His vision blurred.

“One Lunarian,” the lanky one hissed, “freshly awakened Zoan. Maybe we should ask for more for this one.”

And the world went black again.

---

### THE BLACK MARKET OF KRAKE’S MAW

Malphas woke to chains biting into his wrists and ankles. His wings were bound with thick bands of iron. The cage surrounding him sparkled faintly with seastone dust woven into the bars. Every breath felt like he was choking on sand.

He couldn’t move.

Couldn’t ignite.

Couldn’t even stretch his wings.

He looked up. Lantern light struck his face.

He was on a raised platform. An auction stage.

Hundreds watched him—pirates, bandits wearing smiles like cuts in their faces.

The auctioneer’s voice dripped with sleaze. “Our next item—rare! Dangerous! A genuine Lunarian with a mythical zoan! Starting bid—”

A figure in the front row lifted his head slightly.

White garb.

Gold-and-onyx mask.

Still. Watching Malphas with a focus so sharp it looked painful.

Malphas felt uncertainty flicker inside him. The masked man’s fists were clenched so tight the knuckles bled through the glove.

Before the bidding could continue, the two Shadows pushed through from behind the stage.

“Where are the special guests,” the bulky one growled. 

“Did you remember to send the invites?” the lanky one sighed.

The masked man tilted his head. “He looks half-dead.”

“So?” snapped the lanky one. “He’s valuable.”

The masked man responded calmly, voice edged with disdain. “Not that valuable.”

The bulky one snarled and grabbed Malphas by the hair, dragging him forward until Malphas’s forehead hit the cage bars with a metallic clang.

“Maybe this will lower the price,” he said.

The first stab came without warning.

Steel slid under Malphas’s ribs. He gasped, breath escaping in a ragged choke. The second stab punched into his thigh. A third scraped bone.

Pain flared through him—heatless, powerless.

The masked man’s fists trembled.

Malphas hissed through his teeth and slammed his head upward, cracking the Shadow’s jaw with a vicious headbutt. Blood sprayed. The bulky one stumbled back, roaring.

The entire auction hall froze.

Then something shifted in the masked man.

A pressure rippled through the crowd—an aura thick, oppressive, dark.

He stood.

The lanky Shadow moved first. “Sit down, mask-boy,” he spat. “Or you die next.”

A chain shot forward like a whip, aimed at the masked man’s throat.

The masked man didn’t flinch.

Didn’t dodge.

Didn’t need to.

Because the chain never touched him.

A black arm, shaped like smoke-solid muscle, erupted from the air behind him and caught the chain mid-snap. A second voidlimb appeared. Then a third. All writhing behind him like silent, obedient beasts.

The hall erupted in panic.

“DEVIL FRUIT USER!”

“GET BACK!”

“WHAT IS HE?!”

The bulky Shadow charged with a roar, swinging a fist the size of a boulder. Malphas, still against the bars, reached desperately for strength, for flame, for lightning—but the seastone drained everything.

He could only watch.

The masked man stepped into a boxer’s stance, void-arms aligning behind him like wings of shadow.

“You’ve hurt him enough,” he said quietly.

Then he moved.

A black arm shot past him and struck the bulky Shadow’s ribs—crack.

Another coiled around the lanky Shadow’s leg—snap.

A third slammed into the ground, launching the masked man forward like a bullet.

Malphas felt the air vibrate with each hit.

The pirates ran for the doors, screaming. Chairs shattered. The ceiling shook.

The bulky one managed to grab Malphas’s cage and yank it down, trying to use it as a shield. Malphas hit the ground hard, seastone ringing in his bones.

Instinct surged.

The bindings cracked.

Lightning danced along the metal.

The bars exploded outward.

Malphas rose to his feet—wings flaring, electricity bleeding from every feather.

He met the bulky one head-on.

Fists like thunder.

Feathers sparking like storm glass.

Every hit carving out the pain, carving out the fear, carving out the memory of his village burning.

The fight was brutal.

Bloody.

Animal.

Eventually, Malphas’s strength buckled. He dropped to one knee, chest heaving, vision warping from exhaustion and blood loss.

The masked man finished the fight for him.

He crushed the lanky Shadow’s throat between two void-arms.

He drove the bulky one through three stone pillars with a single, brutal punch.

Silence fell.

The masked man stepped over the bodies and knelt beside Malphas.

“You’re hurt,” he said, voice quiet, steady.

Malphas spat blood. “Who… are you?”

The man hesitated, then lifted his mask.

Black wings.

Burning eyes.

A face carved with old battles and harder years.

“My name is Baptiste,” he said.

“Lunarian, like you.”

Malphas stared, stunned.

Baptiste extended a hand.

“Come with me. I sail under a man named Blackhand. He finds people the world tries to erase.”

Malphas swallowed, heart thudding. “My sister… Alice. I need to find her.”

Baptiste nodded once—sharp, certain.

“Then we’ll find her together.”

Malphas took his hand.

And fate shifted.

All zoan type fruits grant the user the ability to shapeshift into the form of a specific animal, either as a full beast or a hybrid form of the beast and their original body.

In beast form, a zoan type inherits all the strengths and weaknesses of the animal side, while in hybrid form they mix the power of their bestial side with the bipedal form of their human side. Most zoans give the user natural weapons, such as the horns of a bull. For the sake of simplicity, any zoan weapon counts as both a natural weapon and unarmed strike.

There are various animals that zoans can transform into, such as various species of cats with regular zoans, extinct species such as dinosaurs with ancient zoans, and dragons from myth with mythical zoans.

Ability Score Increase

Upon eating the fruit, your choice of Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution ability score increases by 1.

Hybrid Form

As a bonus action, you can expend a devil fruit usage to transform into your Hybrid Form, taking the shape that takes the best attributes of both your original body and the beast that now inhabits you. Your transformation lasts up to 10 minutes. This duration increases to 1 hour at 5th level, 8 hours at 10th level, 24 hours at 15th level, and unlimited at 20th level. This transformation ends early if you are killed, or if you end it as a free action.

While in Hybrid Form, you gain the following benefits:

  • When you enter the transformation, you gain temporary hit points equal to your level (double for regular and carnivorous zoans, triple for ancient zoans, and quadruple for mythical zoans).

    All of your attacks deal an extra amount of damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

    You gain any other features from your beast such as natural weapons, enhanced senses, multiple limbs, movement speeds, etc.

    You can speak to other animals of your species. You can still speak your regular language in this form.

Transforming for Roleplay

In the event a player wants to display their zoan transformation for purely roleplay value, such as a brief display of their power to show they are a devil fruit user or just for a comedic display, characters with devil fruits should be able to do so without costing one of their devil fruit resources.



Full Beast Form

As a bonus action, you can expend a devil fruit usage to transform into your Full Beast Form, taking the form of the wild beast that inhabited the fruit you consumed. Your transformation lasts up to 10 minutes. This duration increases to 1 hour at 5th level, 8 hours at 10th level, 24 hours at 15th level, and unlimited at 20th level.

While in Full Beast Form, the following rules apply:

  • Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the Full Beast Stat Block you gain from the fruit, but you retain your alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the creature. The creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus in its stat block. If your physical stats are higher than that of your beast form, you can choose to retain them.

    When you transform, you assume the beast’s hit points and Hit Dice. The hit points of the form scales with your level. For normal and carnivorous zoans it is calculated as (5 x your level) + your Full Beast’s Constitution modifier. For ancient zoans it is calculated as (6 x your level) + your Full Beast’s Constitution modifier. For mythical zoans it is calculated as (7 x your level) + your Full Beast’s Constitution modifier. When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. However, if you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form. For example, if you take 10 damage in Full Beast Form and have only 1 hit point left, you revert and take 9 damage. As long as the excess damage doesn’t reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren’t knocked unconscious.

    You can speak to other animals of your species. You can still speak your regular language in this form.

    You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal. Your equipment changes size or shape to match the new form.

  • You retain the benefit of any features from your class, race, or other source and can use them if the new form is physically capable of doing so. For example, using Extra Attack, Unarmored Movement, Strong Will, Rage, Experimental Medicine, etc.

    Depending on the form, your ability to fulfill the somatic components of creations, use certain equipment like shields, or take actions that require the use of hands may be limited to the DM’s discretion, though through training this limitation may be overcome.

Enhanced Forms

At 10th level, you gain access to a more powerful hybrid form. As a bonus action, you can spend a Devil Fruit usage to access an Enhanced Form Choose either your Hybrid Form or Full Beast Form. You gain the benefits of that chosen form, with a few additional benefits:

  • You can choose to have your size increase by 1 size category, doubling your dimensions and multiplying your weight by 8.

    Your reach with your attacks increases by 5ft.

    Your attacks deal an extra 1d8 damage.

This form lasts 1 hour, and you regain this ability at the end of a long rest.

Endless Forms

Transforming into your base Zoan Forms no longer costs a fruit usage. You can now access your Enhanced form as many times per day as you need, but it still costs a devil fruit usage.
